record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: Is it possible to perform communication-efficient federated training of sub-models while preserving the privacy of which sub-model each client is updating, and what sparsity regimes, private retrieval mechanisms, and secure aggregation variants would make that practical?

evidence.quote: However, when deploying federated learning, communication efﬁciency is often a signiﬁcant concern, leading to the question of whether we can achieve communication-efﬁcient sub-model training. ... Is it possible to achieve communication-efﬁcient sub-model federated learning while also keeping the client’s sub-model choice private?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider a federated learning system with a central server and a set of clients $\{1,2,\dots,N\}$. The global model is partitioned into $M$ disjoint sub-models $\theta = (\theta_1,\dots,\theta_M)$, where $\theta_m \in \mathbb{R}^{d_m}$. Each client $i$ holds local data $\mathcal{D}_i$ that is relevant to exactly one sub-model index $s(i) \in \{1,\dots,M\}$, known only to that client. In each round, client $i$ wishes to (a) download the current value of $\theta_{s(i)}$ from the server, (b) compute a local update $\Delta_{s(i)}^{(i)}$ from $\mathcal{D}_i$, and (c) contribute this update so that the server can form an aggregated update to $\theta_{s(i)}$, without ever revealing $s(i)$ or $\Delta_{s(i)}^{(i)}$ in the clear.

Define a federated sub-model training protocol $\Pi$ to be a multi-round interactive protocol between the server and clients that, at the end of training, produces an updated global model $\hat\theta$. Let $\mathrm{Acc}(\Pi)$ denote the expected utility (e.g., test accuracy) of $\hat\theta$ on the underlying task, and let $\mathrm{Comm}(\Pi)$ denote the total expected per-client communication (uplink plus downlink) per round, measured in bits. Say that $\Pi$ is:
- communication-efficient if $\mathrm{Comm}(\Pi) = o\!\left(\sum_{m=1}^M d_m\right)$ in the relevant asymptotic regime, ideally scaling polynomially in $\max_m d_m$ rather than in the full model dimension;
- index-private if for every pair of clients $i,j$ and every adversary modeled as the server colluding with any subset $T \subset \{1,\dots,N\}\setminus\{i,j\}$ of size at most $t$, the protocol transcript reveals (in either an information-theoretic or a cryptographic sense) no more about $s(i)$ than is implied by aggregate statistics released by the protocol;
- update-private if, in addition, the individual update vector $\Delta_{s(i)}^{(i)}$ is hidden from the same adversary, except through its contribution to the aggregated sums on each sub-model.

Problem. Determine whether there exists a federated sub-model training protocol $\Pi$ that is simultaneously communication-efficient, index-private, and update-private, and that achieves utility $\mathrm{Acc}(\Pi)$ matching (up to a vanishing additive error) the utility of the non-private baseline in which each client sends $\Delta_{s(i)}^{(i)}$ in the clear together with its index $s(i)$. Specifically:

(i) Identify sparsity regimes on $(N, M, d_1,\dots,d_M)$ and on the distribution of indices $\{s(i)\}_{i=1}^N$ (e.g., heavy-tailed versus near-uniform popularity of sub-models) under which such a protocol exists.

(ii) Construct, or prove the impossibility of, a protocol combining a private information retrieval (PIR) or oblivious-RAM-style download mechanism for $\theta_{s(i)}$ with a secure aggregation scheme tolerating up to $t$ colluding parties for the upload of $\Delta_{s(i)}^{(i)}$, whose total communication is sublinear in $\sum_m d_m$.

(iii) Quantify the optimal trade-off, as a function of the sparsity parameters, the collusion threshold $t$, and the desired privacy level, between $\mathrm{Comm}(\Pi)$ and the achievable utility $\mathrm{Acc}(\Pi)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question has stimulated an active research line. Several works (e.g., information-theoretically private federated submodel learning with multiple non-colluding databases, secure-aggregation-based private submodel updates, and hierarchical submodel training) propose protocols that target communication efficiency together with privacy of the submodel index and updates. However, no single protocol is known to simultaneously achieve sublinear communication, full index- and update-privacy under realistic single-server collusion models, and baseline utility across general sparsity regimes; trade-offs are still being mapped, so the broad question remains only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Information-Theoretically Private Federated Submodel Learning with Storage Constrained Databases
status_evidence.snippet: In federated submodel learning, a machine learning model is divided into multiple submodels... the submodel index and update values reveal information about the user's private data, so the model is stored at multiple non-colluding databases to guarantee information-theoretic privacy.
status_evidence.claim: There exist constructions providing information-theoretic index/update privacy for federated submodel learning, but they require multiple non-colluding databases, indicating only partial resolution under restricted models.

status_evidence.title: Federated Learning over Hierarchical Wireless Networks: Training Latency Minimization via Submodel Partitioning
status_evidence.snippet: HIST divides the global model into disjoint partitions so that each group of clients is responsible for training only one partition... saving training time and communication costs.
status_evidence.claim: Communication-efficient submodel training schemes exist, but the cited works do not jointly establish full index/update privacy in the single-server FL setting.
